payload.title: lift_sandbox_pin reads and hashes every tracked path of base_sha from the seat's tree in full, with no size bound and before path admission, so a seat that swaps any tracked non-test file for a huge sparse file exhausts kernel memory instead of being refused by name; every lift also reads all 14,493 tracked blobs (about 149 MiB) of aqua-saas
evidence: aria-kernel/aria_kernel/validation.py:619-632 (the comparison loop: _read_beneath for every base path, listed or not, then blob_object_id over the whole read, before _admit_pin_path)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/validation.py:664 (ls-tree is asked for no sizes (no -l), so nothing bounds a read by the base blob's size)
aria-kernel/aria_kernel/git_object_id.py:90-92 (blob_object_id concatenates header and content (a second copy) and takes bytes, not a stream)
payload.rule_violated: Untrusted input is bounded where it is read (root CLAUDE.md, Security: input validation; ARIA-LOW-972's rule), and a seat's untrusted output is refused by a named error, never by a crash
payload.notes: Registered by the D6-SEC findings clerk from the D6-SEC review round 1 (lens security (with the ssot point on the same reads)), re-checked at head d460f7917 before registration; non-blocking at merge. Close condition: The comparison reads nothing it cannot bound: base sizes come from ls-tree -r -l; a path whose fstat size differs from its base blob's size counts as changed without being read; only a file of equal size is read, never past the base blob's size, and hashed as a stream (no second copy); a changed path's content is read for the pin only after path admission and only up to the pin's file-size limit (ARIA-LOW-972). Tests through the lift: a tracked non-test file replaced by a sparse file larger than the process's address space is refused by name (red_first_pin_path_not_a_test), not MemoryError; a same-size file whose bytes differ is still seen as changed.
